facts.raw_span: A 49-year-old man of Sudanese descent presented with a 5-day history of progressive painful swelling of the face, particularly affecting the eyelids, periorbital tissues, and hands
He took no drugs and had no allergies
He had traveled to Sudan 6 months previously
striking infiltration of the eyelids and periorbital skin with multiple firm tumorous swellings of the forehead and temples
The skin of the forehead, neck, shoulders, and anterior chest had a diffusely rippled appearance
The hands and fingers were swollen with scattered focal purpuric infarcts
C-reactive protein: 43 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L)
No eosinophilia
Normal complement concentrations
Chest radiograph: normal
Dermal oedema and scattered histiocytes
Granulomatous inflammation with intense neutrophilic abscesses in subcutaneous fat
Hale's colloidal iron staining: showed deep dermal mucin
